deepdive.sec: Healthcare / Integrated Diagnostics & Public-Private Radiology Infrastructure

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing internal accruals and debt for Rajasthan rollout; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on ROCE improvement toward 15%+
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Govt payment delays (SNA-SPARSH system issues); receivables cycle extension (150 days); operational disruption from natural disasters (e.g., Punjab/Himachal floods); retail breakeven delayed beyond initial expectations
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, mission-driven, emphasizing scale, quality, and social impact; optimistic on retail and Rajasthan rollout; transparent on working capital issues but dismissive of long-term risk
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Krsnaa’s 36 NABH + 57 NABL + CAP + ACR accreditations create an unmatched quality moat in public diagnostics; retail growth is being funded by PPP cash flows, not equity; senior citizen access is already embedded via PPP, not a separate initiative
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic framing is 'Reach -> Capacity -> Trust -> Cash Conversion', with management explicitly naming the 'next phase' as cash growth / building a larger, more sustainable cash business.
- PPP infrastructure (existing CT/MRI/pathology assets) is leveraged for retail at marginal revenue and minimal incremental fixed cost, framed as delivering superior ROCE.
- Asset-light franchise model - partnerships with local operators, franchise arrangements and collection-centre networks - used to fund expansion without heavy capital outlays.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Radiology: 200+ CT/MRI centers (largest fleet in Asia); Pathology: 57 NABL labs; Retail: 60% QoQ growth, 8% of H1 revenue, targeting 15-20% in FY27; PPP: 18 states covered, 36 NABH radiology centers, India’s first CAP pathology lab in govt facility
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- One of India's largest integrated diagnostic service providers spanning radiology, pathology and tele-radiology, built around the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model for affordable, accessible care.
- One of India's largest NABH-accredited tele-radiology reporting hubs, with capability to process X-rays, CT and MRI scans in real time for patients at the remotest locations.
- Accreditation leader with 120 total NABL+NABH accreditations (66 NABH, 54 NABL) - 2.3x the next-largest tracked peer (Peer A at 53; others range 7-44).
- First-mover credentials: India's 1st ACR-accredited company, 1st NABH-accredited tele-radiology hub, and 1st CAP-accredited lab at a government facility.
- Well-diversified regional revenue mix in Q1 FY27: North 40%, West 39%, South 11%, East 10%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Policy tailwinds] Deck cites sector tailwinds: India's healthcare spend as a share of GDP seen rising from 3.3% to 5% by 2030; MoHFW Budget of Rs 1,017 Bn (Union Budget 2025-26); PM-ABHIM outlay of Rs 42 Bn (FY2025-26); Indian healthcare industry estimated at $1,522 Bn by FY29-30; and a diagnostics TAM of Rs 2.98 Tn by FY30.
- [Contract structure] Long-tenure PPP contracts (radiology ~10+ years, pathology ~5+ years) with a captive government OPD/IPD patient base across district, subdistrict, community and primary healthcare centres.
- [Radiology disruption] The radiology platform continues to expand despite the discontinuation of the Tamil Nadu MRI contract.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 29% via labor productivity, radiology utilization optimization, supply chain efficiency, and automation; retail still loss-making but breakeven expected at ~Rs.100cr revenue
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: higher teens YoY in FY27; margin: sustained 29%+ EBITDA margin; order inflow: pipeline active but undisclosed; capex/commissioning: Rajasthan PPP full rollout by end-Q4FY26, no new equity raise planned
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rajasthan PPP: 10 labs operational by Nov 2025; 25 labs + 500 collection centers by Dec 2025; 152 labs + 1,100 collection centers by end-Q4FY26
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Retail to contribute 40-50% of revenue in 5 years; expansion into wellness/preventive diagnostics; AI-driven reporting and home collection scaling; potential for national PPP tender wins
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Krsnaa delivered 11% YoY revenue growth and 29% EBITDA margin despite PPP contract transitions, driven by retail scaling and operational efficiencies; the imminent Rajasthan PPP rollout by Dec 2025 is the key catalyst for FY27 revenue acceleration and margin uplift.
